faqs.a:
(a)
Only police officers or code enforcement officers are authorized to cause the removal
               of graffiti vandalism pursuant to this article. Once the notice of institution of
               nuisance abatement proceedings has been given to the property owner, and the property
               owner has failed or refused to remove or eradicate the graffiti or request a hearing
               as set forth in
section 38-193
(5), abatement procedures may be commenced.
(b)
The city manager or his designee is authorized to have the graffiti vandalism removed
               or eradicated by appropriate means. Police officers or code enforcement officers and
               those persons designated by the city to execute abatement are expressly authorized
               to enter upon private property for the purpose of causing the removal or eradication
               of graffiti vandalism. The property owner shall be responsible for all costs of abatement,
               including all costs as set forth.
(c)
All assessments and charges imposed under this article shall be a lien against each
               lot or tract of land upon which the graffiti vandalism occurred until paid, and shall
               have priority over all other liens except general taxes and prior special assessments.
               Such lien may be foreclosed upon by the city at any time in the same manner as provided
               pursuant to the provisions of
chapter 59
entitled "municipal liens."
(d)
The abatement and lien procedures set forth in this article for property defaced by
               graffiti shall be exclusive and shall restrict the city from pursuing any criminal
               remedy provided by law.
(Code 1981, § 20-54; Ord. No. 3455, § 3, 7-6-1998;
Ord. No. 4042, § 3, 12-11-2006
)
